mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased cost of capital and reduced risk appetite. The relationship is linear and negative across the observed rate range.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that reduces liquidity and increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.5%, the 20-day forward return is positive, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.3%) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 207) signals a tightening monetary policy cycle that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.3 and CPIAUCSL > 207, the 60-day forward return is positive, or Rank IC for interaction < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5% and is rising (3-month change > 0.1%), it indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5 and UNRATE 3m change > 0.1%, the 20-day forward return is positive, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with stronger economic growth and increased consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and 5-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and 60-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 207.5, it indicates accelerating inflation that triggers monetary policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 207.5, the 5-day forward return is positive, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between strong housing starts (HOUST > 1450) and robust retail sales (RSAFS > 365000) indicates a healthy consumer demand environment that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where HOUST > 1450 and RSAFS > 365000, the 60-day forward return is negative, or Rank IC for interaction < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
